title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)
abstract: arXiv:2611.25985v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The global deployment of autonomous AI agents within and across organisations exceeds the governance infrastructure available to constrain it. Agent communication and authentication protocols, principally the Model Context Protocol and the Agent2Agent Protocol, are maturing quickly, but maturity at the protocol layer does not produce legal legibility at the governance layer. Runtime enforcement written by the deploying organisation fixes the resources an AI agent can reach, not the authority under which it acts. Legal legibility is the capacity of a legal system to recognise, interpret and regulate activity by mapping it onto legal personhood, property, rights and liabilities. Existing (analogue) legal infrastructure cannot supply it for autonomous deployment. The resulting deficit is bidirectional. translated_title: 与AI同速演进的法律：机器时代的关键法律基础设施——法律规制下的自主性架构（AULA）
translated_abstract: 自主AI智能体在组织内部及跨组织的全球部署规模，已经超出了现有可用来约束它们的治理基础设施。智能体通信与认证协议——主要是模型上下文协议（Model Context Protocol）和智能体对智能体协议（Agent2Agent Protocol）——正在快速成熟，但协议层面的成熟并不能在治理层面产生法律可辨识性。由部署组织编写的运行时强制机制只能限定AI智能体可以访问的资源，而非其行动所依据的权限。法律可辨识性是指法律体系通过将活动映射到法律人格、财产、权利与责任之上，从而识别、解释和规制该活动的能力。现有的（模拟时代的）法律基础设施无法为自主部署提供这种能力。由此产生的缺口是双向的：它既涉及当AI智能体造成损害时的责任归属问题，也涉及权利的分配问题，包括数据权利与经济权利等……
tldr: 该论文指出自主AI智能体的全球部署已超出治理基础设施的承载能力，协议层的成熟无法带来治理层的法律可辨识性，由此造成责任归属与权利分配的双向缺口，并提出AULA架构作为机器时代所需的关键法律基础设施。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies a bidirectional "legal legibility" deficit—spanning liability attribution and rights allocation—caused by autonomous AI agent deployment outpacing governance infrastructure, and proposes the Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA) as critical legal infrastructure for the machine age.
